newsitem.title: UK: BP, Mobil say JV to exceed forecasts.
newsitem.headline: BP, Mobil say JV to exceed forecasts.

text.p: British Petroleum Plc and Mobil Corporation said on Friday they expected the benefits from their European joint venture in fuels and lubricants to exceed original estimates.

The joint venture, announced in February this year, will combine both companies' refining and marketing assets in Europe. BP and Mobil said annual benefits were likely to outstrip the original forecasts of between $400 million and $500 million pretax.

In a joint statement, BP and Mobil said they were "delighted with the progress on the joint venture", which was proceeding on schedule on a country-by-country basis and was likely to be completed during the second quarter of next year.

The companies said they expected to reap more than $200 million in divestment proceeds by rationalising marketing assets and selling surplus offices. But they said one-off costs of $740 million before tax would exceed original forecasts.

BP would take exceptional charges before tax of around $490 million and $40 million in fees, expenses and write-downs in the fourth quarter. After tax, the charge would amount to around $430 million, the companies said.

Mobil's costs for restructuring would be around $330 million before tax, resulting in an after-tax charge of around $145 million in the fourth quarter. In addition, Mobil would incur one-off after-tax special charges in 1997 and 1998 of around $110 million.
